entities.summary: Manahen was a Christian presbyter at Antioch in the late 1st century AD, known for his role in the early Christian Church and his involvement with Herod Antipas. Manahen was a teacher and a leader in the Christian community, and his life and teachings have been the subject of scholarly interest and debate. Manahen's significance lies in his contributions to the development of Christian theology and practice, particularly in the area of baptism and the Eucharist. His legacy can be seen in the early Christian Church's organizational structure and liturgical practices, which continued to evolve and adapt over the centuries. Manahen's story serves as a reminder of the importance of early Christian communities in shaping the course of Christian history and theology.
